paper: Exact Transfer of Bounded Linear Recovery and Relative Weight Hierarchies

claims.statement: Under the explicit finite outer gate, the associated relative weights give the sharp rank-stratified confinement thresholds and exact transfer below them; growing outer dual distance gives the eventual family form.
Minimum-weight normalized recovery equations of an MDS code span its dual code.
The restricted helper map gives the stated exact sequence for the associated nested code pair.
The minimum helper-union size for an internally realizable rank-t demand equals the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight of the associated nested pair.
The relative dimension-length profile equals the maximum recoverable target-message dimension from a helper set of bounded size.

For every survivor set, shortening-puncturing duality identifies the unrecovered target dimension with the relative dimension of the dual nested pair on the failed coordinates; its t-th relative generalized Hamming weight is the minimum number of failures leaving t target dimensions ambiguous.
Under the finite outer gate d(O^perp)>r+1 and N>=2, a fixed internally realizable target subspace has the stated sharp confinement threshold; dual-distance growth gives the eventual family form.

Under the finite outer gate, the uniform rank-t nonconfinement helper threshold is the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight plus the inner dual distance; the same holds eventually in outer families of growing dual distance.

Minimizing rank-t helper cost over target t-sets gives the t-th generalized Hamming weight of the dual code minus t, yields the cooperative-locality lower bound, and gives the least eventual first-nonconfinement cost after adding the inner dual distance.

MDS inner codes have the stated exact formulas throughout the recoverable hierarchy, attain the global ceiling when the helper side spans the message space, and first-rank equality in the global ceiling is rigid.
Suitable outer families transfer bounded recovery equations onto positive-density coordinate classes while preserving global asymptotic bounds.

Under the fixed-length outer-dual-distance gate, exact transfer of inclusion-minimal helper supports preserves the bounded service-rate region; outer families with growing dual distance satisfy the gate eventually.
Two represented rank-one recovery systems have the same minimum helper cost and different bounded reliability polynomials.
At every quotient rank, equal complete relative-weight hierarchies can have different full-recovery reliability laws.
Different target coefficient presentations of the same nested helper pair can have different confinement thresholds.
The projective-simplex family has the displayed relative-weight staircase and confinement thresholds.
The projective-simplex family has the displayed rank-reliability and Moebius-inversion formulas.
Equality in the first projective helper-cost bound characterizes the simplex column multiset.
